blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Automatic tools can now generate whole-brain MRI parcellations at cohort scale, but generated-label releases often provide little evidence about which cases are reliable enough to reuse. We introduce OpenBrain, a confidence-aware release of 35,838 provenance-verified OpenNeuro T1w cases from 607 source datasets. OpenBrain is organized as an auditable case-record release rather than a directory of standalone segmentation files: each record links a primary parcellation, two committee parcellations, source/license provenance, raw QC-7 measurements, percentile risks, a combined risk score R, and a confidence tier. QC-7 is a reference-free reliability panel over label geometry, image-label consistency, and committee disagreement, so users can filter, weight, audit, or re-threshold generated labels without rerunning inference. We evaluate this released evidence under a frozen protocol. Across external cohorts, lower QC-7 risk corresponds to higher generated-label quality; in fixed-budget training, lower-risk selections improve paired macro Dice over random selection by +3.2 to +3.7 percentage points. OpenBrain also exposes raw axes, committee outputs, provenance, and datasheet documentation, so confidence claims remain inspectable after download. It does not turn generated labels into manual annotations or clinical-grade segmentations. Its contribution is a large open generated-parcellation substrate, a reusable case-level risk-evidence layer, and an external validation protocol for release-time QC. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/lanqz7766/OpenBrain. Code: https://github.com/lanqz7766/openbrain.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Whole-brain MRI parcellation has reached a point where automatic labels can be generated much faster than humans can review them. Public T1-weighted MRI repositories such as OpenNeuro [ 1 ] provide
large, heterogeneous source cohorts, while automatic segmentation models such as FastSurfer [ 2 ] , QuickNAT [ 3 ] ,
and SynthSeg/SynthSeg+ [ 4 , 5 ] make cohort-scale anatomical labeling practical. That scale creates a release-time problem. Once generated labels are distributed for reuse, downstream users need more than a plausible segmentation file: they need to trace the source scan, inspect likely failure modes, filter or weight cases, and evaluate reuse without manually reviewing every 3D volume.

大型、多样的源组,而FastSurfer[2],QuickNAT[3]等自动分区模型,
和SynthSeg/SynthSeg+ [4, 5] 使组群级解剖标签实用. 这种尺度造成了发布时间问题。 一旦生成的标签被分配用于再利用,下游用户需要的不仅仅是一个可信的分区文件:他们需要追踪源扫描,检查可能的故障模式,过滤器或权重案例,并评价再利用,而无需手动审查每3D卷.

blocks.en:
Existing resources leave two gaps. First, scale, diversity, and whole-brain parcellation labels rarely appear in the same open resource . Manual
benchmarks such as Mindboggle-101 [ 6 ] , the Hammersmith
atlas [ 7 , 8 ] , LPBA40 [ 9 ] ,
and IBSR [ 10 ] remain the appropriate references for
anatomical accuracy, but manual 3D annotation is too time-consuming to scale to tens of thousands of heterogeneous public scans. By contrast, many public segmentation resources provide images, brain masks, tissue labels, lesion labels, or task-specific challenge splits, including pathology-focused benchmarks such as BraTS [ 11 ] , ATLAS [ 12 ] , and ISLES [ 13 ] .

blocks.en:
Second, generated-label releases often lack case-level evidence for reuse. A released label file by itself does not tell users whether the predicted anatomy has visible failure signs, whether independent label generators agree, or whether the case should be prioritized, down-weighted, audited, or excluded. Reference-free QC and uncertainty methods provide useful diagnostics [ 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 , 18 ] ,
and large generated-label releases show that automatic labels can scale [ 19 ] . What remains missing is a documentation methodology for
multi-source whole-brain generated labels: what should be released with each
label so that it can be reused and audited after download?

blocks.en:
A reusable generated-label release therefore needs three properties: source-scale coverage, case-level reliability evidence, and validation that the released evidence supports the decisions it is meant to inform.
OpenBrain is designed around these three requirements. It releases generated whole-brain parcellations for 35,838 provenance-verified T1w cases across 607 OpenNeuro source datasets. The release preserves source identifiers and CC0-compatible public-source provenance, so
derived labels can be traced back to their public sources and reused as a large training and evaluation substrate. Figure 1 summarizes the design shift: OpenBrain releases generated labels as auditable case records rather than as standalone model outputs.

OpenBrain的设计围绕这三项要求. 它释放出在607个OpenNeuro源数据集中35,838个来源验证的T1w病例的全脑包裹. 该发布保留了源识别符和CC0兼容公共来源,所以

blocks.en:
For case-level evidence, OpenBrain releases each case as an
auditable record rather than as a parcellation file alone. The record links the generated whole-brain parcellation to its source provenance and to OpenBrain
QC-7, a compact panel of seven reference-free reliability checks. The QC-7 checks ask three direct questions: does the label geometry look plausible, are the predicted anatomical regions consistent with the image intensities, and do independent parcellation models agree with one another? OpenBrain stores the resulting per-case risk fields and confidence tier in the release case record, so users can filter, weight, audit, or re-threshold cases without rerunning label generation. These fields are not
manual approval labels; they are reusable evidence about where generated labels may be more or less reliable.

Manual and human-reviewed datasets define anatomical targets and remain the right reference for accuracy measurement. In brain MRI, Mindboggle-101 [ 6 ] ,
the Hammersmith atlas family [ 7 , 8 ] ,
LPBA40 [ 9 ] , IBSR [ 10 ] , MALC [ 22 ] , MRBrainS18 [ 25 ] ,
and FeTA [ 26 ] provide manual or expert-curated labels at modest scale. Pathology-focused resources such as BraTS [ 11 ] , ATLAS [ 12 ] , ISLES [ 13 ] , WMH Challenge [ 28 ] , MSSEG [ 29 ] , and ISBI MS [ 30 ] provide human-reviewed lesion or tumor annotations for specific tasks. Larger medical segmentation resources such as AbdomenAtlas [ 31 , 32 ] , TotalSegmentator [ 33 ] , and
TotalSegmentator-MRI [ 34 ] expand scale through automatic tools and human review. These resources provide targets, references, or task-specific annotations. OpenBrain addresses a different setting: generated whole-brain parcellations released at scale across many public MRI sources,
where per-case manual approval is unavailable and release-time reliability evidence must accompany every case.

blocks.en:
Reference-free QC methods provide diagnostics, but their release role differs from OpenBrain. MRIQC [ 14 ] targets raw-image quality rather than generated-label reliability. Reverse-classification accuracy [ 15 , 16 ] estimates segmentation quality without ground truth, but is expensive at large label counts. Test-time augmentation uncertainty [ 17 , 18 ] exposes model instability, but its interpretation depends on the model and domain. UKBOB [ 19 ] is the closest generated-label release
precedent because it scales generated MRI masks and uses filtering plus subset audit. OpenBrain targets multi-source whole-brain parcellation rather than mask
release, and releases the QC axes, percentile risk scores, confidence tiers, and downstream validation as part of the dataset itself, so risk evidence remains available for reuse after download.

present; cases with incomplete QC-7 evidence are excluded rather than imputed,

blocks.en: 6 Discussion

blocks.en:
OpenBrain’s contribution is not another parcellation architecture; it is a
release format for generated labels whose reliability evidence remains visible
after download. Unlike resources that provide manual references, challenge
tasks, or pretrained outputs, OpenBrain releases a large redistributable
whole-brain generated-label corpus with per-case reliability fields
(Appendix B ). QC-7’s value comes
from this record: frozen checks that users can inspect before reuse.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
OpenBrain releases 35,838 provenance-verified generated parcellations with
per-case evidence for reliability, provenance, and reuse. The release is more
than a label collection: it defines a case-record format, exposes three
parcellation outputs, stores raw QC-7 axes and percentile risks, and assigns
confidence tiers that users can reinterpret for their own operating points.
The reusable unit is therefore the case record, not just the label file: users
can keep conservative subsets, down-weight uncertain cases, or revisit
thresholds as validation needs change.
Under frozen choices, QC-7 ranks generated-label quality on external cohorts.
The three-group comparison supports its practical value for fixed-budget
selection over random sampling and identifies a high-risk tail for closer audit. The main claim is
not that generated labels become manual annotations. It is that large
generated-label datasets should ship with visible reliability evidence.
OpenBrain gives one template for whole-brain MRI: scale, provenance, committee
evidence, QC-7 risks, validation, and explicit limits packaged together.

blocks.en: Collection process
blocks.zh: 收集过程

blocks.en:
Data acquisition. Images are selected from public OpenNeuro source
datasets. OpenBrain adds preprocessing, SynthStrip masks, committee
predictions, generated labels, and QC manifests. Human checks guide
pipeline development, QC design, and sampled failure-case review, but
OpenBrain does not add per-case manual label edits to every release case.
blocks.zh:
数据采集. 图像从公开的 OpenNeuro 源选择
数据集。 OpenBrain 添加预处理、 合成口罩、 委员会
预测,生成标签,以及QC显示. 人体检查指南
管道开发、质量控制设计以及抽样的故障个案审查,但
OpenBrain不在每个发布情况下添加每个案例的手动标签编辑.

blocks.en:
Preprocessing. Images are resampled, skull-stripped, and
intensity-normalized before generated-label production. Raw per-axis QC
values are released alongside percentile risks and tiers.

强度在生成标签生产前的常态化。 每轴生 QC
值与百分位风险和分级同时释放。

blocks.en: Uses
blocks.zh: 用途

blocks.en:
Intended uses. Training and evaluating brain parcellation
models, studying reference-free QC, quality-aware sampling, generated-label
correction, and active-learning style data selection.
blocks.zh:
预想用途. 培训和评估人才组合
模型,研究无参考的QC,质量意识取样,生成标签
校正,以及主动学习样式数据选择。

blocks.en:
Unintended uses. Clinical decision-making, diagnosis, and
patient-specific treatment planning. OpenBrain labels are generated labels with
explicit reliability information; they are not clinical-grade outputs.
blocks.zh:
无意用法. 临床决策、诊断和
专门针对病人的治疗规划。 OpenBrain 标签是生成的标签
明确可靠信息;它们不是临床级产出。

blocks.en: Distribution and licensing
blocks.zh: 分发和发放许可证

blocks.en:
Licence. OpenNeuro public datasets are released under CC0 terms after
publication or grace-period release. OpenBrain preserves source dataset
identifiers and citation or acknowledgement metadata in the provenance
manifest, so users can keep source attribution visible in downstream use.

blocks.en: Table 12 summarizes metadata coverage and confidence-tier composition in the full 35,838-case release. The low-risk and flagged subsets are not metadata-matched: flagged cases have older known age on average, a larger male share, more missing age and health-status fields, a higher share of cases marked ill or pathological, and more non-standard acquisition metadata. These differences do not change the role of the tier as a QC-risk label, but they set a clear interpretation boundary. Tier comparisons should be read as reliability comparisons under the released QC policy, not as isolated demographic effects.

blocks.en: Figure 8 first establishes which metadata fields are sufficiently covered, then summarizes mean QC-risk offsets and sampling-arm composition shifts. The clearest mean-risk shifts are associated with acquisition metadata: in the random review pool, 1.5T and 7T/ultra-high-field scans have higher mean QC risk than 3T scans, and Philips and GE scans also show higher risk than Siemens scans. Age groups below 18 and above 65 also have higher QC risk, but these groups are smaller and may be confounded by source dataset and acquisition protocol.
blocks.zh: 图8首先确定哪些元数据字段已充分覆盖,然后汇总平均QC风险抵消和抽样-臂组成变化。 最明显的平均风险转移与获取元数据相关:在随机审查池中,1.5T和7T/超高场扫描的平均值QC风险高于3T扫描,飞利浦和GE扫描显示的风险也高于西门子扫描. 18岁以下和65岁以上年龄组的质量控制风险也较高,但这些年龄组较小,可能被源数据集和获取协议所混淆。

blocks.en: Figure 9 tests whether the subgroup signal is only a mean-offset artifact. The raincloud views show right-shifted distributions for acquisition strata, especially field strength and scanner vendor, while retaining the full case-level spread. We therefore use the random pool for the main subgroup audit and treat lower-risk and higher-risk selection comparisons as a sensitivity check because those selections are selected by QC criteria and are not composition-matched.
blocks.zh: 图9测试该分组信号是否只是中位落的文物. 雨云视图显示采购层的右转分布,特别是外地兵力和扫描仪供应商,同时保留整个案例的分布。 因此,我们利用随机集合进行主要分组审计,并将低风险和高风险选择比较作为灵敏度检查,因为这些选择是根据质量控制标准选择的,没有与组成相称。

blocks.en: Overall, this audit supports a limited conclusion. Available metadata can help identify where generated labels need closer inspection, but the current evidence does not support a demographic fairness claim. The strongest use of this analysis is to document acquisition-linked reliability differences and to motivate source-dataset-aware evaluation protocols.
blocks.zh: 总的来说,这一审计支持有限的结论。 现有的元数据可以帮助确定哪些地方生成的标签需要更仔细的检查,但目前的证据不能支持人口公正主张. 这种分析的最强用途是记录与获取相关的可靠性差异,并激励对源数据集-认识的评价协议.
